assignments.title: Privileged access review
assignments.resultSummary: Privileged access review answered part of the question and raised others.

messages.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
messages.subject: A programme has stalled
messages.body: One of your programmes has not moved in three weeks. The blocker is not technical and it is not money. It needs somebody senior to make a decision.

messages.subject: SOC contract renewal decision required
messages.body: Sentinel's contract renews in eight weeks and I need a direction from you. Renewing as-is is straightforward. Anything else takes time I need to start spending now.

messages.subject: The CIO wants the security conditions eased
messages.body: Two delivery teams have raised that security review is now the longest step in their release process. I am not asking you to drop it. I am asking whether it has to look like this.

messages.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
messages.subject: Some legacy systems are not backed up at all
messages.body: A sample showed 23 legacy systems outside the central backup schedule, including two that support despatch. The systems least able to defend themselves are also the least recoverable.

messages.subject: She remembered what you said you did not know
messages.body: When you gave me your three risks in your first month, you told me which of them you were unsure about. I have had cause to repeat that to the board, and it has done you no harm at all. Tell me what you are unsure about now.

messages.subject: Cloud migration slips again
messages.body:
The migration has slipped another quarter. The remaining legacy workloads are harder than the survey suggested and we have lost two engineers to the platform team.

I know what this does to your legacy exposure. I do not have a better answer today.

messages.subject: Sustained scanning of the partner portal
messages.body: Automated scanning against the partner portal has run continuously for six days from a rotating set of addresses. Nothing has succeeded. Yet.

messages.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
messages.subject: Container workloads can read the customer store
messages.body: Workloads on the shared cluster inherit a platform role with broad read access to production data stores. Any compromised workload becomes a data problem.

messages.subject: A merchant is asking about card data handling
messages.body: One of the larger merchants has asked, in writing, for confirmation that card data is not retained outside the payment environment. I would like to answer accurately.

messages.subject: Briefing: patient collection against data platforms
messages.body: A government briefing describes an actor collecting behavioural and commercial data sets from analytics providers over periods of a year or more. Detection in the reported cases came from partners, not from the victims.

messages.subject: Nordic market: local payments partner selected
messages.body: We have signed a local payments partner for the Nordic entry. Integration work starts next month. I assume there is nothing here that should worry us.

messages.subject: Closed-account data is being kept indefinitely
messages.body: Records for closed accounts are retained indefinitely in the analytics estate, contrary to our published retention policy. I have been told this is a technical limitation. I do not believe that is the whole story.

messages.subject: Warehouse systems named in a vendor advisory
messages.body: The vendor of the Meridian warehouse platform has issued an advisory for a remotely exploitable flaw. There is no patch for the version we run, and there will not be one.

messages.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
messages.subject: A quiet week
messages.body: Nothing to escalate this week. Worth noting, because it does not happen often and because it is the right time to do something you have been putting off.

messages.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
messages.subject: The logistics integration has write access
messages.body: Lattice Logistics' integration account can write to and delete records in order management. The integration only ever needed to read them.

messages.subject: Where you started
messages.body: You came to the service owners first, before anything else. Six months on they still bring things to you directly rather than through the change process, which is either a compliment or a problem depending on the week.

messages.subject: Something is probing the test environment
messages.body: An exposed service in the non-production tenancy is being probed persistently. It is only a test environment, which is the reason nobody has looked at what it can reach.

messages.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
messages.subject: The board wants a risk appetite statement
messages.body: The committee has asked for a cyber risk appetite statement. I would like something we could actually test a decision against, rather than three paragraphs about being risk-aware.

messages.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
messages.subject: Card data outside the payment environment
messages.body: A discovery scan found unencrypted card data in two application log stores outside the defined payment environment. The regulated boundary is wider than the one we have been describing.

messages.subject: Credential campaign against sector portals
messages.body: A sustained credential-stuffing campaign is running against partner portals in this sector. Volumes are high and the operators are patient about lockout thresholds.

messages.subject: People Cloud discloses an incident
messages.body: Our HR provider has notified customers of unauthorised access to a support system. The notification is vague about scope and firm about there being no evidence of customer data access.

messages.subject: You waved the launch through
messages.body: You backed the launch without conditions and I have not forgotten it. My people took that as permission to move at the same speed on the next two integrations. I am telling you because you will want to know before you find them.

messages.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
messages.subject: A new starter, and a reminder
messages.body: Our new identity engineer starts on Monday. They will take about two months to be useful, which is worth remembering before we commit them to anything.

messages.subject: A supplier in the sector has been compromised
messages.body: A managed service provider serving several businesses in this sector has disclosed a compromise. Corvus is not named. Corvus uses the same remote access product.

messages.from: Sir Alan Whitcombe, Chair, Board Risk Committee
messages.subject: First quarter closes
messages.body:
You have had a quarter. At the next committee I would like to hear what you now believe, what you have changed your mind about, and what you still cannot answer.

I am more interested in the third of those than the first two.

messages.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
messages.subject: A project you had not heard of
messages.body: The commercial team have been running a customer data enrichment project with an external provider for four months. Nobody told us. The data flows out of the analytics estate nightly.

messages.subject: An enterprise client is asking security questions
messages.body: One of the Insight Services clients has sent a 140-question security assessment as part of their renewal. Some of the questions I cannot answer honestly and confidently at the same time.

messages.subject: Third sector ransomware case this quarter
messages.body: A third comparable business has been extorted this quarter. Two of the three were reached through a managed service provider's privileged access. The tradecraft is consistent and unremarkable, which is what makes it effective.

messages.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
messages.subject: Partner accounts live in the staff directory
messages.body: Partner identities for the extranet are held in the same identity platform, and the same tenant, as employee accounts. A partner credential compromise starts from inside our identity boundary.

messages.subject: High-severity alert turns out to be a printer
messages.body: The cluster of high-severity alerts from the corporate network overnight was a misconfigured print server running a nightly discovery scan. Four analyst hours.

messages.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
messages.subject: Backups share credentials with what they protect
messages.body: The backup platform is administered with the same privileged accounts as the systems it backs up. An actor with production administration would be able to remove the recovery path and the systems together.

messages.subject: Blocker: Executive exemption requests
messages.body: Three executives have asked to be exempted from the new privileged access flow. Their assistants have already escalated.

messages.subject: Targeted phishing against finance
messages.body: Eleven finance staff received a convincing invoice lure this morning. Two opened it. One entered credentials. The account has been reset.

messages.subject: Nexora credentials found in a breach dump
messages.body: Sixty-two corporate email addresses with passwords appear in a credential dump from an unrelated breach. Nine match accounts that are still active here.

messages.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
messages.subject: Annual penetration test: scope decision
messages.body: The testers want scope confirmed. Last year's engagement excluded the legacy data centre on cost grounds, which is convenient given it is the part I understand least.

messages.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
messages.subject: An observation from your SOC lead
messages.body: Something I have noticed: we spend most of our time on the estate we can see, which is the estate that was built recently and properly. The parts I worry about are the parts we have no telemetry for, so they never appear on any of our reports.

messages.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
messages.subject: What do we do about standing supplier access?
messages.body: We now have it documented: fourteen permanent privileged accounts belonging to Corvus, no expiry, no second factor. Procurement will help if we give them something specific. Operations will resist anything that touches night cover.

messages.subject: Due diligence window on Kestrel
messages.body: There is a window before completion where technical due diligence is still possible. It closes in about six weeks. After that, integration planning takes over.

messages.subject: The warehouse platform question
messages.body:
I am told the Meridian platform is running on software that is no longer supported. I am also told it cannot be upgraded and that migration is at least a year away.

Despatch runs on it. Three sites. If it stops, we stop. What are you proposing to do about that?

messages.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
messages.subject: Remediation is the constraint, not detection
messages.body: Median time to remediate a critical finding on production is 94 days. We are very good at finding things. We are not resourced to fix them.

messages.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
messages.subject: A programme has stalled
messages.body: One of your programmes has not moved in three weeks. The blocker is not technical and it is not money. It needs somebody senior to make a decision.

messages.subject: A competitor has been breached
messages.body: One of our competitors has lost customer data and it is on the front page. The board will ask me on Thursday whether it could happen to us. I would like a better answer than 'possibly'.

messages.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
messages.subject: Two documents, two different answers
messages.body: The architecture pack says the legacy estate is fully segregated from production. The firewall rule base says otherwise. Both are current documents.

messages.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
messages.subject: An access review failed
messages.body: A sample access review on order management found nine leavers with active accounts and two accounts with rights nobody could explain. The reviewer had approved the previous round without reading it.

messages.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
messages.subject: The questionnaire was wrong
messages.body: Corvus told us their privileged access enforces multi-factor authentication. I checked the remote access configuration this morning. It does not, and it never has.

messages.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
messages.subject: Escalation quality review
messages.body: Of 340 escalations last quarter, 318 were false positives. The team has started closing them without reading properly. That is a control failure, and it is ours rather than the provider's.

messages.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
messages.subject: 412 service accounts, no owners
messages.body: 412 non-human accounts. 78 have passwords older than five years. 31 hold privileged rights. Nobody owns them, which means nobody can safely remove them.

messages.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
messages.subject: Threat hunt found nothing
messages.body: The hunt came back clean. That is genuinely good news, with the caveat that we hunted where we have telemetry, which is not everywhere.

messages.subject: A four-hour outage, nothing to do with security
messages.body: Order management was down for four hours this morning. Database failure, no security dimension, but the executive will ask you anyway because it was an outage and you are the new person.

messages.subject: Working exploit published for the checkout framework
messages.body: Proof-of-concept code was published overnight for the framework version running our checkout service. It is reliable and it is already being used opportunistically.

messages.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
messages.subject: Your architecture lead went further than asked
messages.body: While mapping dependencies I also pulled the firewall rule base. There are rules between the legacy estate and production that nobody can account for. I have documented them.

messages.subject: Sustained scanning of the partner portal
messages.body: Automated scanning against the partner portal has run continuously for six days from a rotating set of addresses. Nothing has succeeded. Yet.

messages.subject: External audit: privileged access, third year running
messages.body:
The auditors have raised privileged access management again. That is three consecutive years, and the audit committee has noticed.

I need a response from you for the committee papers. Please do not send me the same remediation plan we sent last year.

messages.from: Stefan Alvarez, Head of Security Architecture
messages.subject: Nobody can say what is in the legacy data centre
messages.body: Three asset lists disagree on how many systems remain in the legacy estate. The range is between 60 and 140. Two of them are in the backup schedule. We think.

messages.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
messages.subject: A quiet week
messages.body: Nothing to escalate this week. Worth noting, because it does not happen often and because it is the right time to do something you have been putting off.

messages.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
messages.subject: The incident response plan names someone who left
messages.body: The plan names an incident commander who left in March. It has not been exercised in two years. If something happens tomorrow, we will be inventing the process while using it.

messages.subject: Release cadence is increasing
messages.body: We are moving to twice-weekly releases on the platform. I am telling you rather than asking, but I would rather you heard it from me.

messages.subject: Anomalous vendor access, three nights running
messages.body: Vendor remote access sessions at 03:40 on three consecutive nights, outside Corvus's contracted hours. Analyst confidence is low; the account behaviour is not conclusively abnormal. Raising it because the pattern is consistent.

messages.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
messages.subject: Publicly readable storage in production
messages.body: Two storage buckets in the production tenancy permit anonymous read. One contains application logs including session identifiers. They have been like this for at least seven months.

messages.from: Jo Mbeki, Head of Security Operations
messages.subject: The last restore test was abandoned
messages.body: I went looking for the last recovery test report. The test was abandoned after eleven hours and the report was never reissued. Fourteen months ago.

messages.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
messages.subject: The privileged vault covers a third of administrators
messages.body: The vault was bought two years ago and deployed to about a third of administrators. Adoption stopped at the point the infrastructure team objected to session recording, and nobody pushed.

messages.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
messages.subject: Corvus returns a clean questionnaire
messages.body:
Corvus has returned the annual assurance questionnaire fully compliant, including enforced multi-factor authentication for all privileged access.

I would like to believe it. I have not tested it.

messages.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
messages.subject: The MFA exception register
messages.body: 214 accounts sit on the multi-factor exception register. Most were granted as temporary. The oldest is three years old. Nineteen of them are administrative.

messages.subject: Credential campaign against sector portals
messages.body: A sustained credential-stuffing campaign is running against partner portals in this sector. Volumes are high and the operators are patient about lockout thresholds.

messages.subject: Completed: Privileged access review
messages.body: Privileged access review answered part of the question and raised others.

messages.subject: Targeted phishing against finance
messages.body: Eleven finance staff received a convincing invoice lure this morning. Two opened it. One entered credentials. The account has been reset.

messages.subject: Sign-off requested: new customer platform
messages.body:
We are on track for launch and I need your sign-off in the pack. The date is public, the marketing spend is committed, and the board has been told.

I am not expecting a problem. If there is one, I need to know this week, not the week before launch.

messages.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
messages.subject: Two vacancies, six months open
messages.body: Both identity engineering roles are still open. We have been covering with the people we have, and it is starting to show in what we can commit to.

messages.subject: High-severity alert turns out to be a printer
messages.body: The cluster of high-severity alerts from the corporate network overnight was a misconfigured print server running a nightly discovery scan. Four analyst hours.

messages.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
messages.subject: The inherited risk register
messages.body:
Twenty-three open entries. Nineteen have not been updated in eighteen months. Several describe systems that have since been decommissioned, and at least two describe controls that were subsequently switched off.

I would not read it as a description of where we are. I would read it as a description of what somebody was worried about in 2024.

messages.subject: Third sector ransomware case this quarter
messages.body: A third comparable business has been extorted this quarter. Two of the three were reached through a managed service provider's privileged access. The tradecraft is consistent and unremarkable, which is what makes it effective.

messages.from: Callum Reid, Head of Security Engineering
messages.subject: 6,283 critical vulnerabilities
messages.body:
The number people keep quoting at you is real. It is also close to meaningless: about a third sit on an isolated development cluster with no inbound routes and no real data.

Eleven of them are on internet-facing services. Those are the ones I would look at.

messages.from: Fenella Osei, Head of Cyber Risk and Governance
messages.subject: Your leadership team
messages.body:
Four of us report to you: security operations, security architecture, cyber risk and governance, and security engineering.

A warning before you start assigning work. Everyone here is already committed. If you give us more, something else stops, or it comes back thinner than you wanted. We would rather you chose than we quietly disappointed you.

messages.subject: Your three risks
messages.body: You have had one morning. I have five minutes. Tell me what you have.

messages.subject: The CEO meeting starts in 23 minutes
messages.body:
Welcome aboard. I have twenty-three minutes and one question: what are the three cyber risks I should be most concerned about?

You have inherited 6,283 critical vulnerabilities, 17 high-priority audit findings, 23 open risk register entries, four transformation programmes, fourteen important suppliers and five security vacancies.

Where do you start?

messages.subject: Your first day
messages.body:
08:07, Monday. Your first day as CISO of Nexora Group.

The CEO meeting starts in 23 minutes. She wants to know what the three cyber risks she should be most concerned about are.

What you have inherited: 6,283 critical vulnerabilities, 17 high-priority audit findings, 23 open risk register entries, four major transformation programmes, fourteen important suppliers, five security vacancies and a cyber budget that looked generous until you saw the estate.

What you do not have: a picture of how any of it fits together.

asm-1.statement: The payment platform's exposure does not change materially this year.

entries.summary: Where do you start?: Start with the business services
The CEO wants your three risks: Give her your three, and say how confident you are in each
Five vacancies and a long recruitment cycle: Recruit properly
Security conditions on the platform launch: Support the launch as planned
Started Identity and privileged access uplift with 850k.
Out-of-hours vendor access: Commission a focused threat hunt
The repeat audit finding: Commit to a funded programme with dates
A working exploit for the checkout framework: Force an emergency patch
The legacy warehouse platform: Isolate it properly
Standing supplier access: Remove standing access immediately
Penetration test scope: Include the legacy estate
The HR provider's incident: Press them for specifics
Customer data held beyond policy: Enforce the retention policy
Card data outside the payment environment: Fix it and tell the acquirer
The SOC contract renewal: Renew as-is

quarters.boardReaction: The board accepted the papers, but 1 material item was not on the agenda. They will find out another way.
